title: Reading about signed documents
page_title: Signing records you can trust later

blocks.text: A signed record is only useful if someone can trust it months later, when the person who signed it isn't in the room. A few habits make that much easier.
Sign at the moment of capture
Sign the record where it was made, at the time it was made. A signature added later, after the record has traveled through a few systems, says less about what was actually seen.
Store the time of signing with the record itself, not the time it was received or uploaded. If a device was offline for a day, those two times can be far apart, and only one of them matters.
Never edit a signed record in place. If something was wrong, make a new record that corrects it and points back to the original. Both stay readable.
The original shows what was known at the time.
The correction shows what changed and who changed it.
Print a short check value on the record, derived from its contents. Anyone reviewing it later can recompute the value and confirm the file hasn't changed since it was signed.
None of this needs to be complicated. Most of it is deciding early that a signed record is finished.
